detail.body:
## Summary

Fix Muon scaling when distributed GTP tensors contain alignment padding. Newton–Schulz still uses the padded tensor for collectives, while the scale factor now uses:

`logical_rows = local_rows × gtp_size - pad_length`

## Background

GTP shards weights along dimension 0. When the row count cannot be divided into equally sized, alignment-compatible shards, GTP appends zero rows before sharding.

For instance, the 16-row per-rank alignment would add paddings as follows:

- `[126, N]` with GTP8 is padded to `[128, N]`, giving each rank 16 rows.
- `[62, N]` with GTP8 is also padded to `[128, N]`; some ranks contain only padding.
- `[124, N]` with TP4 × GTP2 is first split into 31-row TP slices, then each slice is padded to 32 rows.

These zeros are required for storage and communication, but must not affect Muon’s logical shape or update scale.

## Test cases covered

| Layout | Padded shape | Logical shape | Spectral scale |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GTP2 | `[8, 4]` | `[6, 4]` | `2.828 → 2.449` |
| TP2 × GTP4 | `[16, 8]` | `[13, 8]` | `4.000 → 3.606` |
| TP4 × GTP2 | `[32, 8]` | `[20, 8]` | `5.657 → 4.472` | 

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [x] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Note
This MR is actually a following up fix for [MR-6740](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6740/changes#diff-1b1a6333750ab7d324aa4b5d859161dabeb37f9e98c7bed27f94ba7d57760e3eR293-R294) (fix(gtp+muon): strip GTP_remat alignment padding before Muon orthogonalization) which only strip the gtp-padding (if has) for blockwise and duplicated mode before scaled_orthogonalize_fn but did not cover distributed mode by design

+def _worker_padded_distributed_parity(
+    rank, world_size, port, tp_size, gtp_remat_size, logical_m, partition_dim
+):
+    """Padded distributed NS must match unpadded full-matrix NS and Muon scaling."""
+    _init_model_parallel(tp_size, gtp_remat_size)
+    try:
+        pgc = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+        opt = _make_muon(pgc)
+        w = _full_weight(logical_m)
+        ref = _reference_full_orth(opt, w, pgc.tp)
+
+        gs, gr = _world_size(pgc.gtp_remat), _rank(pgc.gtp_remat)
+        ts, tr = _world_size(pgc.tp), _rank(pgc.tp)
+
+        if partition_dim == 0:
+            # Column-parallel TP owns a contiguous logical row block. GTP pads and shards
+            # each TP block independently, so the padding is repeated once per TP rank.
+            assert logical_m % ts == 0
+            logical_m_per_tp = logical_m // ts
+            pad_length = (-logical_m_per_tp) % (_PAD_ALIGNMENT * gs)
+            tp_start = tr * logical_m_per_tp
+            tp_w = w[tp_start : tp_start + logical_m_per_tp]
+            tp_ref = ref[tp_start : tp_start + logical_m_per_tp]
+            padded_w = torch.nn.functional.pad(tp_w, (0, 0, 0, pad_length))
+            padded_ref = torch.nn.functional.pad(tp_ref, (0, 0, 0, pad_length))
+            shard_rows = padded_w.size(0) // gs
+            local = padded_w[gr * shard_rows : (gr + 1) * shard_rows].clone()
+            expected = padded_ref[gr * shard_rows : (gr + 1) * shard_rows]
+        else:
+            # With TP absent or partitioning dim 1, every TP rank sees the same logical rows;
+            # the one GTP pad is followed by the optional TP column slice.
+            pad_length = (-logical_m) % (_PAD_ALIGNMENT * gs)
+            padded_w = torch.nn.functional.pad(w, (0, 0, 0, pad_length))
+            padded_ref = torch.nn.functional.pad(ref, (0, 0, 0, pad_length))
+            shard_rows = padded_w.size(0) // gs
+            local = padded_w[gr * shard_rows : (gr + 1) * shard_rows]
+            expected = padded_ref[gr * shard_rows : (gr + 1) * shard_rows]
+            if partition_dim == 1:
+                assert _K % ts == 0
+                shard_cols = _K // ts
+                local = local[:, tr * shard_cols : (tr + 1) * shard_cols]
+                expected = expected[:, tr * shard_cols : (tr + 1) * shard_cols]
+            local = local.clone()
+
+        assert pad_length > 0, "test shape must exercise real GTP alignment padding"
+        local.is_gtp_weight_remat = True
+        local.pad_length = pad_length
+
+        out = opt.scaled_orthogonalize_fn_with_gtp_remat(local, local, pgc.tp, partition_dim)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected, atol=_ATOL, rtol=_RTOL)
+    finally:
+        ps.destroy_model_parallel()
+        ps.initialize_model_parallel()
+

+def test_muon_optimizer_gtp_distributed_padding_uses_logical_scale_shape(monkeypatch, scale_mode):
+    """Distributed NS keeps aligned rows, but Muon scaling uses the logical matrix shape."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace

+

reviews.body:
Light review. The core fix is correct: I worked through all three `partition_dim` cases and the logical-shape derivation holds, including the non-obvious column-parallel one where GTP pads each TP slice independently so the pad appears `tp_size` times in the reassembled matrix — multiplying `size[0]` (already pad-corrected once) by `tp_size` is the right composition there, and `test_padded_distributed_parity[column-parallel]` pins it against real collectives.

Test coverage is solid: mocked unit tests for the scale-factor arithmetic across all three `scale_mode` values, plus real-collective parity tests including the `gtp-only-padding-spans-shards` case where `pad_length` exceeds one shard.

One comment posted, on the docstring dropping `(known limitation)` while `split_qkv` views remain uncorrected.

## Light review

Read the diff, `megatron/core/optimizer/emerging_optimizers.py` in context, and the `mcore-testing` skill.

**The fix looks correct.** The `scale_shape` override is threaded only into the final `get_muon_scale_factor` call and deliberately leaves `grad`/`partition_dim` untouched, so the NS collectives keep the physical padded layout they need. I checked the shape math against all four parametrized layouts and it reconstructs the logical shape in each:

- `partition_dim=None` / `1`: `local * gtp - pad` recovers the full logical dim-0, and the `size[partition_dim] *= tp_size` on dim 1 restores the columns.
- `partition_dim=0`: GTP pads each TP dim-0 block independently, so `pad` is per-TP-block and the `*= tp_size` correctly re-multiplies the already-unpadded per-TP row count. Applying the pad subtraction before the TP multiply is the right order here — the reverse would undercount by `tp_size x pad`.

The `grad.shape != p.shape` guard is a good addition: `pad_length` comes off `p` while the row count comes off `grad`, so that invariant is exactly what makes the formula valid, and it is checked rather than assumed.

**Test coverage is solid** and directly targets the regression: the `gtp-only-padding-spans-shards` case (`logical_m=62`, GTP8) covers the section 3.7 Case B layout where padding spills backward past the tail rank, both TP x GTP directions are covered, and the unit tests assert `expected_scale != padded_scale` so they would fail if the override silently stopped applying. The `assert pad_length > 0` guards keep the shapes from quietly drifting into a no-padding configuration that tests nothing.

No GPU kernel is added or changed here — the diff only alters which scalar multiplies the NS output — so the `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/` requirement does not apply.

Two minor comments inline (one stale docstring, one missing test guard); neither affects the fix itself.

### Optional

`docs/api-guide/core/generalized_tensor_parallel.md` section 1.6 and the `test_gtp_muon.py` row of the section 4 test table do not mention padding for the Muon modes, so nothing there is made inaccurate by this change. But since section 3.7's closing trade-off already lists "a bookkeeping tax on every raw-buffer consumer", Muon's scale factor is now another such consumer, and a line in 1.6 would give this fix the same discoverability the split-QKV rule has. Your call — not a blocker.
